chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from Zurara from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them)

Regarding a man who divorces his wife with one divorce, then leaves her until three months pass except for one day, then he reverts to her in a gathering, then divorces her, then did that again at the end of the three months as well
He said, so he said: When he enters the reversion, she observes the waiting period with the last divorce, and when he divorces without reversion, the divorce does not occur for him

key_terms.رَجْعَة: Revocation of divorce (taking back the wife during the waiting period)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of a divorce if the husband's revocation of the first divorce is deemed invalid?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Zurarah, elucidates the precise mechanics of *raj'ah* (unilateral revocation) in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that the validity of the revocation determines whether the subsequent divorce is effective. It highlights the scholarly distinction between a valid revocation, which resets the *iddah* clock to the final act, and an invalid one, which nullifies the divorce entirely, reflecting the rigorous attention to procedural integrity in *fiqh al-ahwal al-shakhsiyyah*.
